newsitem.title: CROATIA: Tudjman says Croatia would send suspects to Hague.
newsitem.headline: Tudjman says Croatia would send suspects to Hague.

text.p: Croatian President Franjo Tudjman said on Thursday any indicted war crimes suspects found in Croatia would be extradited to The Hague and said he would encourage Bosnian Croats to do the same.

"Whoever has been indicted and is present in the Republic of Croatia will be delivered to the tribunal in The Hague but in Croatia there are no indicted persons held by the Croatian authorities," Tudjman told Reuters in an interview at his presidential palace in Zagreb.
"It is only Croatia that has done everything, that whoever was indicted and was in the Republic of Croatia was sent to The Hague. No other side has done so," he added.

When asked whether he planned to use his influence over Bosnian Croats to encourage them to extradite indicted suspects living in the staunchly pro-Croat region of Herzegovina, Tudjman said: "certainly...But I cannot be held responsible for what is taking place in Bosnia Herzegovina.
"So far we have also brought our influence to bear on the situation over there and...I believe the results were more than good."

Croatia has been harshly criticised by the United States and its Western allies for not doing enough to ensure indicted suspects are sent to the international tribunal in The Hague, set up by the United Nations Security Council in May 1993.
It has indicted 75 war crimes suspects -- 54 Serbs, one of whom has died, 18 Croats and three Moslems -- but has only nine in its custody.

The World Bank indefinitely postponed a $30 million loan to Croatia on Tuesday after strong lobbying from the United States, which said Croatia had not met commitments made in peace agreements over issues including war criminals.
Croatia extradited Zlatko Aleksovski to the court in April, the first time it had handed over a suspect, after coming under serious pressure from the United States.
